newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Edgars says H1 shr to remain constrained.
newsitem.headline: Edgars says H1 shr to remain constrained.

text.p: South African clothing retailer, Edgars Stores Ltd, said on Tuesday that business in the first six months of its new financial year would remain tight amid expected continued subdued economic activity.

"No meaningful upturn in economic activity or consumer spending is expected until short term interest rates decline, consumers reduce their currently high levels of debt and their confidence returns," Edgars said in a statement accompanying year end results.
"As a result, business in the first six months is expected to remain constrained."

However, should the consumption of semi-durables start to recover in the second half of the year, when the bulk of profits are made, there could be limited growth in sales and earnings for the year as a whole, the group said.

Edgars reported attributable earnings for the year to end March down five percent at 320.9 million rand. The group said low volume increases and the negative gap between inflation in operating costs and that inherent in merchandise prices brought margins under pressure.
